utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm so sorry. May I just mention three very short matters before we return to the witness? There's a reason for wanting one of the matters mentioned early, with Your Honours' leave. The matter that I need to mention early is Antonic-Simic because of travel arrangements. As I forecast yesterday, our position is that we would not ourselves think it necessary to call her, but in view of the overall position on this evidence, I think it is my duty to tender her for cross-examination should the accused so desire, and I would need to know his reaction to that really now in order that travel arrangements could be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, do you want to cross-examine Mrs. Simic? It's a matter for you. We've heard what she said in the statement, but if you want to ask her some additional questions, you can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that can be taken as evidence at all for and concerning the statement of General Markovic, of course I would like to cross-examine her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Let her be called.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll deal with the other matters later this morning. It's probably better.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Witness K41, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to keep you waiting. There are just one or two administrative matters we've got to deal with. It's nothing to do with your evidence. All right? Yes. What is it, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also would like to broach a topic. Yesterday, you explained in this courtroom -- that is to say you mentioned witness Kevin Curtis. In his written statement, there are new facts, factors, such that he asked and, without any papers at all, unlawfully seized me out of Yugoslavia with the help of the representative of the Ministry of Justice and police. Second, the new facts that he is talking about are that the base of the American army in Tuzla took part in this, which is where I was, and that also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I'm not going to argue about this now. We've given a ruling that he is not to be called, and that means he won't be called. Now, we have a witness here who is waiting to give evidence on the videolink. We will hear the witness. We will hear any submissions -- we'll hear any submissions you want to make in due course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to broach another topic. It is your duty, in conformity with the rules and regulations, to look into the matter of my unlawful arrest in light of the facts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we're not hearing legal submissions now. We will hear from you in due course. Right now we're going to hear this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Witness K41, we're going to hear your evidence. Could I remind that you took the solemn declaration yesterday and that, of course, still applies today to your evidence. Could I remind you, too, that you're going to hear questions from counsel here. What has got to be said has got to be interpreted, so would you bear that in mind and pause. As far as the arrangements are concerned today, the Albanian booth is not operating for technical reasons. It's not been possible to connect it, and doing so led to technical difficulties yesterday. Now, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. You'll recall that I had about three questions proposed in closed session before the technological problems that prevented that. May we start? Just two more questions, in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness K41, just a couple of preliminary questions, if I may. Do you have a criminal record? And by that I mean have you ever gone to court, been convicted of a criminal offence, and sentenced for that by a judge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hold a passport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have, therefore, a passport to enable you to travel to The Hague to testify on relatively short notice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to get a passport because the time was too short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that applications for passports are obtained through the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason why you were reluctant to go to the police station to apply for a passport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was one reason, slight one, why I didn't go there, and the reason was that some two months ago they came to me, to my home, and my brother told me that they were looking for me, and then I asked my relatives to help me and solve this problem, because I didn't know what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you subsequently learned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the problem? Why don't you put your headphones on? Can we see if -- can we go on to make sure the accused can hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've just told us that the police came to your home about two months ago looking for you and spoke to your brother. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. They didn't say why they were looking for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, is that the reason why you have not gone to the police station to apply for a passport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of the reasons too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: The interpreter is very loud, but his voice is absolutely not understandable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've done the best we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I might, the witness is speaking in the Serbian language, which the accused understands. I don't know whether an interpreter is necessary. If the accused would wear the earphones, he would hear the voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Do you hear that, Mr. Milosevic? Put the headphones on, or listen in on the headphones, and you can hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have placed them, but I can't hear. It is the Serbian that I cannot hear, Mr. Ryneveld. I don't know whether Mr. Tapuskovic can hear the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear the Serbian very well, Your Honours, but I don't hear the interpretation from the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I suspect that perhaps the Serbian comes in in different channels, so what channel does the Serbian come in on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Listen, we must get on with this. We cannot waste further time arguing about channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's go on and see how -- whether the accused can hear all right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do I understand, sir, that you started your compulsory national military service on the 17th of March, 1998 with the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did your particular training take before you were dispatched to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The training took 3 months and 20 days, and we stayed on until the 9th of September, when we became part of the 549th Motorised Brigade in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander of the 549th Motorised Brigade in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander was Colonel Bozidar Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you, as part of that unit, happen to know the brigade's area of responsibility? And if so, after you name the places, could you show the Court on the map that you have available the area that was under the 549th Brigade's responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can show you the area. I think I can show you on the map. And it came under the responsibility of the 549th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. At the bottom corner we see Prizren, and that's where you were stationed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could name --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prizren --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our area of responsibility was Suva Reka, Orahovac up to the border, Dragas, and the environs of Prizren. I can indicate this for you on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do. All right. We now see a larger version of the map. You're pointing to Prizren. Could --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of responsibility was Prizren, Suva Reka, Orahovac. And I'm going to show you -- let me just move the map a bit. There was also Dragas, right up to the border there, the border with Albania. That was our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And within the brigade, I understand that there is a battalion. It's Battalion Technical Company. Is that where you were particularly assigned to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was assigned to that Technical Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of work did you do with that Technical Company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Technical Company was in charge of maintenance of trucks, although up to December we also engaged in road construction, and we dug channels for water for the border huts. We would ensure food supplies and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I neglected to ask you earlier. When you joined the 549th Motorised Brigade, how old were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was 19 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that within the brigade there was a sub-unit called a battalion, and you were in that particular battalion. That was called the Logistics Battalion. Can you tell me who was the leader or the commander of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the battalion to which I belonged was Captain First Class Pavle Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Technical Company within that battalion, who was in charge of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the command of Jacimovic, Dragisa Jacimovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there also field operations carried out by your Technical Company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when that occurred, who, if anyone, took charge during those operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those operations were taken charge of by Sergeant Kozlina, Rajko Kozlina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, how long did you remain with the company in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained in Prizren up until the 10th of June, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that time period between the 9th of September, 1998, and the 10th of June, 1999, were you ever involved, personally involved, in field operations including military operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did take part on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may just ask you, do you recall being involved in a place called Ljubizda Has?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did take part in that operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could ask you to turn to the Kosovo atlas, page 10. Could you show us on that atlas where that location is? All right. You're now looking at page 10. Perhaps we could get that focused a little clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you're watching on your copy, it's at the intersection of 5 at the top and 24 on the right-hand column. So centre of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think you have it now, Witness. Fine. In any event, can you tell us what, if anything, you were told before engaging in that military operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we engaged in the operation, we said we were -- they told us that we were just going to have a demonstration of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- briefly, what in fact happened and when did it occur? When did this operation take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That military operation took place -- I think it was in December. And we were told that we would be going to demonstrate our might. But when we arrived at the village, we saw that there was no demonstration of might or power of any kind. And when we came to Ljubizda Has, we passed through the village, and we went beyond the village and we set up an ambush there. And they told us that anybody coming into the village was to be shot at. And we remained there the whole day until nightfall. And in the evening, we withdrew to the first houses in the village. And it is from these houses that we were told -- we were told to expel the people from houses. And after that, when the people had been expelled from their houses, we took our positions in the houses and spent the night there. In the morning, once again we went back to our positions at the ambush spot, and we stayed there until the following night. And after that, we withdrew once again and went back to barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions for clarification, if I may. Who told you to do the things that you have described to the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The military police was there, and this lieutenant colonel - I think Konjikovac was his last name - they said we should return to the village in the evening and that we should expel the people from their house so that we would take their place and spend the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, it needs to be clarified who "we" is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. That was about to be my next question. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, sir, was "we"? Who were you with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We soldiers who belonged to the Technical Company. That's what I meant when I used the word "we."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And were there any officers in charge of your particular unit on that particular military operation; and if so, who were they, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officer who was with us in this operation was a sergeant who we called Vodja, the leader in this particular action, but I don't remember his exact name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just so that I'm clear: You were part of the VJ, the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe in your evidence you indicated that the military police were also involved. Is that correct or did I misunderstand you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just so that I'm clear: Is it your evidence that the army and the police were there together; and if so, who expelled the persons from their homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While we were in the ambush above the village, as the Technical Company, we were separate from the military police. The military police was stationed down in the village. And in the evening, when we returned down to the village, the military police and we -- I mean, we were ordered, together with the military police, to expel the people from the village, and then the military police escorted them out of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. All right. And were you subsequently involved in another campaign in February of 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part in that campaign. As far as I can remember, it was in Jeskovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, with reference to the Kosovo atlas which you have with you there, could you turn to page 14 and point out to Their Honours, if you would, please, where Jeskovo village is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, to assist, M26 on page 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have the map there. You're pointing -- do you find Jeskovo on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it. Let me just move the map. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You're pointing to the place called Jeskovo. And is that south of Prizren, sir? It's hard to tell on map 14. Is that south of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes, it is south of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you describe, sir, in a brief way, if you would, what happened with respect to the village of Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Jeskovo, we were placed on the alert sometime around 3.00, after midnight. We did not know exactly where we were going. The next day, when they transferred us by trucks to above the village of Jeskovo, our commander, the captain, said to us that this was an operation, that about 700 of us soldiers were taking part in this, and also that special units of the police were taking part in it. And when we took up positions above the village of Jeskovo, then the artillery started, the tanks, anti-aircraft guns. They all started shooting at the village. Later on, when this artillery shelling subsided, finished, then we set out to clean up the village, and that lasted until the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you understand it to mean when you were told to, as you now put it, clean up the village? What did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We understood that no one should remain alive in the village, because we were told that there is no one there except for soldiers who belong to the KLA, the KLA, as they were called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your subsequent experience, did that turn out to be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understood things, and as far as I saw things in this action, perhaps I saw about ten dead persons, but I did not see a single one in a KLA uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us, sir, that some military equipment was shooting at the village, and then once that subsided, you were told to go clean up the village. Can you tell us what kind of military equipment was used to shell the village prior to you going into the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military equipment that was brought there involved tanks. It also involved three-barrel anti-aircraft guns and also Pragas. This is also a type of anti-aircraft weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you may have said. Are you able to estimate how long this shelling of the village took place before you went in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, about half an hour, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during either the shelling phase or the time when you and other soldiers went into the village to clean it up, did you ever notice any return fire from the direction of the village? In other words, was there any shooting at you and your fellow soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the village, I did not notice any fire coming at us, except for when we ran into the village, the soldiers who were behind us started shooting. We did not know what this was all about. We thought that it was some of these KLA soldiers, but we realised that somebody had hid in the woods behind us, and the soldiers saw this man and started shooting at him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see that man; and could you tell us, if so, if he was wearing a uniform or any insignia at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He wore a civilian uniform. And when he got out of the bushes, walking towards them, he held his hands up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you personally saw about ten bodies. Do you know, from what you found out from fellow soldiers, or other information, about how many people were killed in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I found out, in that operation I think that about 30 people lost their lives. I saw, I think, at least ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness K41. I'm going to ask you now to turn your mind to the last week of March of 1999. Do you recall Captain Gavrilovic giving instructions to your company to do anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that happened in the month of March during the night. I do not remember the exact date, but I know it was night-time when the NATO bombing started. That night, around 9.00 or 10.00, Captain Gavrilovic came to the battalion, and he ordered the soldiers to be issued uniforms, ammunition, and equipment that they need for combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you in fact issued with those uniforms and equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you leave immediately or did you leave the following morning, in the early hours of the following morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not leave immediately. We left in the morning hours, the following morning, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go and how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can we make it plain from the outset -- sorry to interrupt you, Witness K41, but it's important we make it plain from the outset who the witness is referring to when he says "we"? It is not clear and it should be clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, throughout when we've been talking about "we," are you talking about you and other soldiers who were part of the 549th Motorised Brigade of the VJ army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am speaking about soldiers who were with me in my company and also in the Logistics Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again I apologise if I've asked you this before: What was Captain Gavrilovic's position in regard to your group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Captain Gavrilovic, what was his position with respect to the army? What was he in charge of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was commander of the Logistics Battalion. He was responsible for the Logistics Battalion in the rear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of which you were a part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll return to my earlier question. In the early morning hours of the following day after the NATO bombing news reached you, where did you go and how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We entered the trucks and we went through a village, a Serb village. I think it's called Novake. And we arrived at a hill above Trnje, to the south of Trnje. That's where we arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to turn to page 11, if you would, of the atlas. Along the left hand margin of that page, about centre of the page. Make sure the left margin of the page is showing, please. Not the top, the left. Yes. Thank you. A little bit higher, please. A little bit more. There we are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we can clarify that. Now, there's Suva Reka visible at the top. And do you see Trnje and Novake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Novake is a Serb village before Trnje, on the southern side, right over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how far away is that from Trnje, which is just about --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, about half an inch up on the page from Novake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is that, sir, approximately? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember exactly how far away it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is perhaps a kilometre or two away. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What time of the morning did you get there approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was around 4.00 in the morning, something like that. 3.00, 4.00. The early morning hours. That's what I do know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And was there any heavy artillery or military equipment with you and your group, from the 549th with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our group there, the Logistics Battalion, the only heavy weapon, if it is a heavy weapon, is an anti-aircraft gun which is called the three-barrelled gun. And we only had that gun, which we positioned on this hill above Trnje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you would, please, can you tell us that morning, overlooking Trnje, who were the people in charge who were present? Who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, to the officers, the ones with us were Pavle Gavrilovic, the commander of the battalion, his deputy Gligorevic, and there was Jacimovic, and there were the sergeants who were in charge of their platoons. That is Rajko Kozlina, Delic, and Fejzic. Miroslav is what we called him. I don't know his exact name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was your immediate commander? In other words, who was the sergeant who was immediately in charge of the group in which you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our immediate superior was Sergeant Rajko Kozlina, who took over command in such situations when going into action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any police with you on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On that occasion, there was only one policeman. I think he was from the Serb village of Novake. He was probably familiar with the terrain, and that's why they dispatched him together with us, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was -- this operation appeared to be almost entirely military with one policeman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've mentioned a number of superior officers including sergeants. Can you give the Court an estimate of approximately how large a group of soldiers were involved in this military operation? How many companies or how many groups for a total number of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember now, there were three companies, three sergeants who led their platoons in companies, and I think it involved 80 to 100 soldiers, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on your arrival about 3.00 or 4.00 in the morning, you've told us basically what you did, and can you tell us in your own words basically what happened? When did things start happening and who did what? Just tell us your narrative, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning when we came to that hill, we disembarked from the trucks, and the trucks were positioned so they could not be seen from the village on the hill. On the hill, this anti-aircraft gun was positioned, the three-barrelled gun, the way we called it, and then it could target the village. After that, we waited up on the hill with our sergeants. We stood there, and Captain Gavrilovic called the sergeants to issue some order to them. The sergeants walked from us to Captain Gavrilovic, and he asked them whether they and their soldiers were ready for action, and they answered yes to him. After that, he motioned with his hand towards Trnje, and he said that on that day no one should remain alive there. And the sergeants, when they understood the order that he issued to them, they turned to us, our sergeant turned to us, and said to put our company together, and then he set out in front of us, downhill, towards Trnje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where were you when this order was given by Captain Gavrilovic to the sergeants? Were you within hearing distance of this, personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was about three or four metres away from Captain Gavrilovic and Sergeant Kozlina. There were also other soldiers there who were around me and who could clearly hear the orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, after this order was given, sir, what, if anything, happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this order was issued, the sergeants, Kozlina and Nedeljkovic, set out towards the village of Trnje with their companies, and Sergeant Fejzic remained on the hill with his soldiers. Afterwards, as we were going downhill, all the soldiers realised what this was all about. We knew. We were getting close to the village. As we were getting close to the village, we were spreading our ranks in order to be in combat position around the village. As we were taking our positions on the periphery of the village, there was a man who was walking with some bag on his shoulder, on his back. Probably he had some cattle feed or something. A burst of gunfire was fired from next to me, and this man fell. After that, we took up positions there on the outskirts, and after a while the anti-aircraft gun started firing at the village. This lasted for about 20 minutes. And then, after that, we set out into the village. The first thing we did was that we set on fire a haystack that was on the way, and after that we saw people in two columns. One group was fleeing towards Lesane and the other ones were fleeing to the left, towards the stream.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. Mr. Ryneveld, it would be really helpful and it would clarify matters if you would not lead, but take the witness through this account.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. What I had originally planned to do is let him do his narrative and then back up and fill in details, but if you'd rather I did it piece by piece, I certainly will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's just back up for a moment and fill in some details, if we can, sir. As you went to the village, you've told us about an old man, and you heard a shot and the man fell. Do you know who shot the man, the man carrying the cattle feed, or the bag that you assumed ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sergeant shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sergeant?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter kindly requests the witness to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sergeant Kozlina, who was our sergeant, shot at him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you told us about the three-barrelled anti-aircraft weapon shelling the village. And during that shelling, or at some later time, did you see whether there were any occupants of that village, of Trnje, and what, if anything, they were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The villagers I saw were indeed fleeing - I said a while ago - to the left-hand side, towards Lesane and the other group -- no. To the right towards Lesane, and others were fleeing to the left, towards the stream. I mean left and right of us, as we were moving along, as we had taken up our positions facing the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And perhaps if you could turn to the atlas again. Would you have the atlas, please, again at page 11. You've earlier shown us where Trnje is on page 11. Can you point out where ^ Lesane is? Just move the atlas a little bit to the right so that we have the left-hand margin available. Yes. Okay. Do you see Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the village of Trnje, and to the right is the village of Lesane, to the right of Trnje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right, sir. Now, what were you doing while the shelling was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While the shelling was going on, I and the other soldiers who were standing next to me, to my left and right, took up our positions and waiting for the shelling to stop, in order to be able to enter the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the shelling stopped, did you receive instructions from anyone to do anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The sergeant, Sergeant Kozlina, got up, and to the left and right of him, the soldiers started moving. And we said, "What's up?" And they said, "We're on the move," which meant that we were moving into the village. Right after him, after he started, we followed. When I say "him," I mean the sergeant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: En route into the village, after the shelling, did you encounter anyone? In other words, did you see any other people? And if so, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we started towards the village, there was a man running between the houses, 300 or 400 metres away, or in front of us, and we heard a burst of gunfire and the man fell to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who shot him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the first thing that you or your company did once you got to the village, after this man was shot? Let me direct your attention to your earlier evidence. I think you talked about a haystack.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first thing that happened, what I said earlier on, was that we set fire to that haystack. And later on in groups, two by two or three of us went into the houses in the village, and the houses were set fire to one by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On whose instruction did that occur, if anyone's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the instructions issued by our sergeant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I am in fact going to stop you now, Mr. Ryneveld. It's right that I should give the witness a formal warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K41 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K41, I must just tell you this formally. You've been told it before, but it should be repeated. You are not obliged to give evidence which would incriminate you of any offences. You may, of course, do so, but unless you're ordered to do so, you're not obliged to give the evidence. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partially. I apologise, but I didn't quite understand. Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You do not have to give evidence which would incriminate you, which means it would admit -- which admits on your part any criminal offences. And you're now dealing with setting houses on fire, and there may be other matters you're going to deal with in which you admit criminal offences in which you participated. You do not have to give that evidence, but of course you may do so. You don't have to unless you're ordered to do so. You should understand your legal position. Yes, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. Yes. Thank you. I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Despite the formal warning given by His Honour, do you still wish to continue to answer my questions about what occurred on that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I said so previously in my statement. I have come here to testify, to speak about what I saw and heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Sir, we're to the point now where you've told us that you went from house to house. What were you doing in the process of going from house to house? What were you looking for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This searching of houses, what we were doing was looking to see that nobody remained in the houses. And we went in groups. The sergeant would issue orders to each group, the two or three of us, to go into the houses and to check and see whether there was anybody left inside. If there was nobody left inside, then we were to burn the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the first ten or 15 or so houses that you encountered, did you find anyone inside in the group in which you were a participant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our group did not find anybody in those first ten or so houses that we entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did -- I think you've already answered this question, but when you found no one in those houses, you set fire to them, I take it. Is that what you told us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were searching houses, do you recall an incident involving an elderly man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. I remember an elderly man who was forced out of his house, and I remember the sergeant ordering the soldier to shoot at him. But the soldier refused and said, "I can't do it. I can't shoot at the man." And I also remember that he killed him with a burst of gunfire, shooting at his head, and said, "This is how it's done."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I could ask some questions for clarification. Who was the -- who was the sergeant and who was the soldier involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sergeant was Kozlina, and the soldier was Private Milosevic, who didn't want to shoot and who said, "I can't shoot."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Private Milosevic that you knew, had you -- had you known him while you were in your training? Was he, like you, a recent recruit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met Private Milosevic in Prizren when I arrived there, when I was placed under the command of the 549th Motorised Brigade. That's when I met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Private Milosevic said, "I can't," who shot this old man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sergeant Kozlina shot him with a burst of gunfire from an automatic weapon and said, "This is how it's done."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what effect shooting at him had on the old man? In other words, was he injured or killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The old man fell down, and I think he was dead. I don't think. I'm more than certain that he fell down dead because he remained lying on the ground there and we continued on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, happened to his house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His house was set on fire like all the other houses that the army came across.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you continue going from house to house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us about an incident that you recall where -- the first instance where you found someone in a home you searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we came to one particular house, we saw the curtains move on the windows of the house, and we knew that there was somebody in the house. So we entered the yard, and in the yard there was a house on the left-hand side and some garages, and there was some houses on the right-hand side. I and several other soldiers went into the right-hand side houses, and the people who were in the houses were expelled. They were forced out into the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom and how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were brought out by the soldiers who entered the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you one of those soldiers who did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was with the soldiers who went into the right-hand side house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they taken out at gunpoint or some other way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course at gunpoint. There was a gun placed to each of their heads when the door was opened, because we were told that possibly there were soldiers belonging to the KLA there too. But there was nobody there except the civilians who were in the houses. And at gunpoint they were told to leave their house and go outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how many people they were and what their gender or ages would have been approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on when they were all assembled in the yard and when they were told to sit down in the yard, I think there were about 15 people there. There were women there too, children. I remember at least one child that I saw. And there were some elderly people too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any babies? Is that what you refer to as the child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I mean. There was at least one baby. It might have been -- well, not even a year old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, were the people told to do once they went outside or do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the people had left their houses and gone outside, our sergeant was there and they ordered them -- he ordered them to sit, to sit down in the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next he told a soldier to take one of the men out, one of the men who was sitting down there, to take him to the garage and to ask him whether they had any money on them. And when the soldier told him that they didn't have any money, he told the man to go back to his position in the yard and to sit down. And he ordered the soldier to go back to where the rest of us were standing, and he said -- he told the rest of the soldiers who were in the courtyard to move towards the gate, to leave the yard and go towards the gate. And the four or five of us who remained there, he told us to stay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just so that I'm clear, originally we have more than four or five of you. There were a number of soldiers in the courtyard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were more soldiers, and there were some soldiers who were still in the houses, and there were other soldiers who went into the yard later on to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I understand your evidence correctly that Sergeant Kozlina ordered most of the soldiers to head towards the gate, leaving four or five of you behind in the courtyard with the civilians? Is that -- do I understand it correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was. He told the soldiers, the other soldiers apart from us, four or five, he told the rest of the soldiers to get out of the yard, to leave the yard, and they moved towards the exit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question before we continue. At any time were these civilians questioned by anyone, other than the request for money? Were they asked at all about KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They asked them where the KLA was, whether there were any KLA members there, and I remember them saying that there was never any KLA there and that there was nobody belonging to the KLA there. And then there was a round of swearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you told us about the man who was taken aside and put back in place in the yard. You told us that the soldiers were -- most of the soldiers were ordered out of the courtyard, leaving four or five of you behind. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question, because what I received as translation was that one soldier left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. All right. Let me repeat my question. You've told us that a number of soldiers were sent out, leaving four or five of you behind. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rest of the soldiers started to leave the yard, and the four of us, or five of us, remained. And our sergeant, Sergeant Kozlina, who was there, ordered us to shoot the people who were in the yard, the people that sat before us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who shot the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sergeant who was there shot, and all the remaining soldiers, the soldiers who stayed on there, shot, the four or five of us, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you shoot at all of the civilians in front of you? When I say "you," I mean collectively the group.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Our group shot at the people who were there. Each from the position he was in shot at all the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, do you recall happening to the people at whom you and your fellow soldiers shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were shot at began falling down one across the other, one over the other, and what I remember most vividly is how -- I remember this very vividly. There was a baby, and it had been shot with three bullets, and it was screaming unbelievably loud.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you believe happened to those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I wanted to do was to get out of that place as fast as possible, and Sergeant Kozlina, when we left the place, told us soldiers, the two or three of us who were in that group, that we should check the other house on the left-hand side to see that there wasn't anybody in that. And in the house on the right, there was an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go into that house, the other house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Soldiers had searched the house beforehand, and we saw this old man there who had been killed, who was dead. There was nobody else in the house. So we left the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came out of that house, where did you go and what did you hear, or what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all left the house and left the yard. And it was on the main road, actually. The main road went through the village. One of the soldiers said that you could see the curtains moving in another house. After a certain amount of time, the window was broken on that house and a bomb or grenade was thrown inside. And after the explosion, nothing further was heard in that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you moved on to different houses in the village after that incident of the 15 or so civilians; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you left --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you left the compound with the civilians who your group shot, did you see whether any other soldiers checked to see what had happened? Did you see anyone looking in the courtyard at all and then leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as the shooting stopped, there were soldiers in the yard. Soldiers entered the yard to look around, because both the companies had collected there already. And so somebody came out -- the soldiers went to see what had happened, and then we continued on our way towards a nearby shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when you got to the nearby shop? What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: We're at paragraph 20, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they told us that we could take what we needed from the shop: food, drink. If we were thirsty, we would take some fruit juices; we would take some food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is "they"? Who told you you could do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our sergeant told us that directly. The sergeant of our company said we could go and help ourselves, because we would not be getting any food coming in to us, any rations, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the soldiers do when they were told they could do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to the shop, and everybody helped themselves, took what they wanted or needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to stop here, sir. During this whole incident so far, from when you arrived at the village of Trnje overlooking the hill, during the shelling, and then during the events that you've just described to us, did you at any time see return fire coming from the village? Was anyone shooting at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At no point was there any shooting or opening of fire from the village, nor did we come across any uniforms or rifles which would mean that there had been soldiers belonging to the KLA there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After helping yourselves to the goods in this shop, did you leave the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We moved towards the bridge, which is north of the village. So we left the village and went in the direction of the bridge. On the left-hand side you could see seven or eight women who had just been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that vantage point, were you able to see any VJ military equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the bridge, you could see a tank and a Praga, and they had been positioned some 500 metres north of Trnje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These women, could you tell how they had met their death? Were they drowned, or could you tell how they died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The women who were there by the roadside, in the field, were quite -- had quite obviously been shot with bullets fired from an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to head into a different topic at paragraph 22. Would this be a convenient time or would you like me to continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We started rather late.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Fine. I'll continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Go on for another quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you've told us that there was a bridge. I take it there was also a creek. The bridge went over a stream of water, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did something happen? Well, what happened next? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we crossed that bridge. We started walking along that creek, and perhaps 200 or 300 metres from that bridge there was a group of people that had sought shelter from the village by that creek. There was a primitive bridge that they had placed there. It was just a log. And there were 30 or 40 people there. I heard shouting. I heard the soldiers shouting that they should all surrender or that otherwise they would be killed. However, Lieutenant Jacimovic, who happened to be there, practically started besieging them to let the women and children go. And that is what was done. The women and children were released, and also a disabled man who did not have a leg. The remaining persons, that is to say four or five men, were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to give us an estimate of the range of age of these four or five remaining men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These men who remained I think were, say, between 40 and 50 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they killed and by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment when they were shot at, I was about ten metres away, because I tried to be as far away as possible from my superiors so that I would not get any other similar orders that I would have to shoot. So I was about ten metres away. And both companies were there. There were a lot of soldiers, so I could not see exactly who shot at them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what happened next, sir? Did you go to -- did you continue on and go towards another village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, we went on for another 200 metres or so and there we got some rest. And then we helped ourselves to what had been taken from the shop. After that, when we got our rest, our sergeant and about ten of us soldiers went to a hill facing the village of Mamusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we pause there, and can I ask you to just turn the page from page 11 to page 10 of the Kosovo atlas that you have there. And you will see that because we're on page 11 we're on the left-hand margin. There's the same area depicted on the right-hand margin on page 10. Do you see Trnje right under number 22 on the right-hand column there? We have to move it. There we go. 21. Up a bit, please. Do you see Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Point it out. All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see Mamusa just immediately to the left of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Left of Trnje, Mamusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to Trnje, followed the stream, and then you -- you and about ten other soldiers, under the leadership of Sergeant Kozlina, do I understand, went towards Mamusa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We continued along the creek for about 200 metres, and then we took a break there and then we proceeded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we went towards Mamusa, to the right of the stream, that is, and we came to this elevation from which Mamusa can be seen, and that is where we stopped then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were having your rest and while you were eating the stuff stolen from the shop, could you hear anything happening in respect to the village of Mamusa in relation to the anti-aircraft weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we took a break and when we went up to this elevation, about ten of us and our sergeant took up positions above Mamusa, and that is when this anti-aircraft gun started engaging the first seven or eight houses that were on the outskirts of Mamusa. And afterwards, when this shelling ended of these seven or eight houses, we set out to these houses, and we were told that these houses that had been shelled should be torched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The houses that had been shelled were torched, and the sergeant and we returned to that elevation where we had been during the shelling of those houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any other soldiers who were with you in that group? Now, you've earlier referred to a Private Milosevic who had told Kozlina he couldn't shoot the man. Was that person with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which man are you referring to when you say that there was a man or, rather, person with us?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You recall telling us that Sergeant Kozlina showed a soldier how it was done by shooting an old man, and that person who said he couldn't do it you said was Private Milosevic. Do you now know what I'm talking about? Earlier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that Private Milosevic with you in the group that went to Mamusa or do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall anybody else by name who may have been with you in that group? If not, just say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that group that went to Mamusa, I could not remember the names of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been three years now, and I do not remember some of the details any longer, but I do remember quite a few details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In any event, after you then burned these houses in Mamusa, did you return to Trnje that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When these houses were burned when we returned from the stream where our group of about ten soldiers and sergeant had set out, we reached them and it was dark. It started getting dark. And we were told that we should go back to the hill where Captain Gavrilovic had remained, and we were supposed to go back to them. And then we crossed the bridge in Trnje, and there when we entered Trnje, we saw that some people had come back because of the cigarettes that were still burning. And there was a man who was right in front of us, and the sergeant called him, and he walked up and he said that he had just come from Lesane, that he didn't know anything, and that he's not guilty of anything. The other one didn't answer him at all, he just shot him. And then there was a lot of commotion in the dark. Other people could be seen round those cigarettes that could be seen, that were still burning. And then the soldiers, we started shooting around. And after that we were ordered to go back to where we had been, going through Trnje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of quick questions on that point. I believe you said you saw cigarettes and that it was dark. Were these people smoking these cigarettes or were these cigarette butts that had fallen on the ground or what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw people who were smoking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we saw the movements they were making with their hands as they had cigarettes in their hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you tell their ethnicity by what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were ethnic Albanians, because the man who had been killed wore their traditional cap on his head. What's its name now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just for clarification, you said, and I'm looking at the transcript, you said, "There was a man who was right in front of us, and the sergeant called him and he walked up and he said that he had just come from Lesane, that he didn't know anything and that he's not guilty of anything." Yes, translate that first. And then you said: "The other one didn't answer him at all. He just shot him." Who are you talking about, "the other one," and who shot who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant that the sergeant did not give him any answer to his explanations that he had come from Lesane and that he was not guilty of anything. The sergeant ordered him to come, did not give any further clarifications to him, did not talk to him at all. He simply shot him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, will you be moving on now to another topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I will be, yes, Your Honour. Paragraph 27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K41, we're going to adjourn now for a break. That will be for 20 minutes. Could you remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence during the break, and that includes people from the Prosecution, and not to speak about your evidence until it's over. We will adjourn now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, just before the break, I understood that you stayed in Trnje for a period of time. Is that correct? How long did you stay in Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "how long"? Are you referring to our entire stay?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. After the shooting incident you talked about, where the old man wearing the Albanian cap was shot, you went back to Trnje, and how long did you then stay in the Trnje area? Do you remember? If not, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that incident when this old man was killed, there was shooting there, and then there was commotion. And then the sergeant said that we should go back to where we had been and that that is where we would spend the night, over there where we had rested, by the river, and that's where we returned after that incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to touch very briefly on the next couple of incidents. Was there an incident involving two men coming along the road from Mamusa to Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the last day when we were there. When we crossed this bridge, we returned to the hill. We joined up with the soldiers who had stayed behind with Captain Gavrilovic and Fejzic's company that had remained on the hill. When we reached them, somebody noticed that two young men -- they were probably young men. That's what it looked like, judging from their walk. We were told that they were walking from Mamusa towards Trnje. And when they reached the place where we had spent those days while we were there by the river, when they arrived at that spot, the army started shooting at them. They fell on the ground, and we could hear them shouting from down there, "Don't shoot, soldiers. Don't shoot, soldiers." And when this was heard --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand who --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- said that the shooting should start. One of the two men who were lying on the ground, one of them started running towards the creek, and the other one put his hands up and started walking towards us. The one who had started running towards the creek was targeted by the anti-aircraft gun that was on the hill, and the other one, who had raised his hands, came about 80 metres away from us, and at that moment, Sergeant Fejzic reached Sergeant Kozlina. He came up to him, talked to him, and then Sergeant Fejzic proceeded further on towards the man who was coming towards us. And when he was perhaps about ten metres away from him, he shot at him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could clarify that incident briefly, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, sir: Were you present -- was there any discussion between Sergeant Kozlina and Sergeant Fejzic prior to the shooting of this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were jokes. Sergeant Kozlina was saying, "Fejzic, here, you've got an opportunity now to have your name inscribed as well now." It was our understanding that that meant that he was probably supposed to shoot someone too. And the other one proceeded past us and went about 20 metres away from us and then shot at this man who held his hands up. And after that, he turned around, smiling, as if he had done something good perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I believe you told us earlier that Fejzic's company had stayed behind on the hill, while Kozlina's company and another company had gone into Trnje to, as you phrased it, clean up the village. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after this shooting incident where Fejzic shoots the man who was surrendering, did you return to Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After that, we remained on the hill. And afterwards, we returned to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you left and you went to Prizren. The following day what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The following day, we were told -- we were told that we were going to Trnje when we boarded the truck. We left on a military truck, and there was also a civilian truck that was following us. And we were told that if we saw anyone along the way we should shoot them, or if there was anybody in Trnje or outside Trnje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that? Who told you to shoot people along the way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what we were told by Sergeant Kozlina. Sergeant Kozlina said this to us. He said that if we saw someone along the way that we should shoot them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And "we," the company, battalion, the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are you talking about, sir? You got onto this military truck with a group of soldiers. Who were the soldiers? Whose company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sergeant Kozlina was in this military truck, and his Technical Company was on the truck as well, the soldiers from his Technical Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were among those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You refer to a civilian truck. Was that also from your company or was that from a different company or driven by someone from a different company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it belonged to, the civilian truck. I cannot know who it belonged to. It just followed us. And we did not -- I mean, the main point is that it followed us, and I cannot know and I cannot say who it belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you happen to know who drove that truck? Was it a civilian or was it a soldier or what? Or do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That truck, I think that Sergeant Nedeljkovic was on it and some of the soldiers. I can't remember who actually drove it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And -- because later on when we arrived in Trnje, Sergeant Nedeljkovic got out of the truck. I remember that. And he gave us gloves and sacks in order to collect the dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you collecting the dead from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, when we came to Trnje, we entered the yard that I told you about earlier where that group of people had been killed. In that yard there was no one except for blood where they had been. On the ground there was blood. And then we proceeded towards the meadow, to the bridge where those women were lying. There were about five or six bodies of these women there. And what was also visible were places where there were one or two bodies that had been taken as well. The sergeant told us that the bodies of the men who were killed in the creek should not be touched, that they should remain, that only the women's bodies should be collected and those of children as well if any were found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took these sacks. We collected these women, and we boarded them onto the civilian truck and started out towards Prizren and returned further towards Zur up there where they were taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And Zur is near the border with what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is near the Albanian border, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the interests of time, I don't -- I'll just direct Your Honours' attention to page 14, K26, but I'm going to continue if I may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got to -- you drove towards Prizren? Where did you go to? What kind of an area was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean what kind of an area?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll be --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What area?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll be more specific. You left the village of Trnje with a truck full of bodies of women and children and then you drove somewhere. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got out after Trnje to the road between Suva Reka and Prizren, and that's the road we took all the way to Prizren. And then I think that other soldiers joined up there from the Logistics Battalion. To be more precise, from Nedeljkovic's company, those who were providing additional security. Then from Prizren we set out towards Zur, and I think that from Zur we went somewhere into those hills. We got there in these trucks, and that is where we buried these bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in a formal graveyard or was it on an asphalt road, or did you go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that we took the asphalt road to Zur, and then through these hills we took macadam roads, and then about 50 or 100 metres - I can't remember exactly - we drove into some bushes in the mountains, and we dug a hole, where the bodies where thrown in and then covered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why the bodies were taken into a bush area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, probably so that they wouldn't be found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. All right, sir. And then afterwards, did you return to your barracks or did you go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that we returned to Prizren. We did not return to the barracks. We returned to the town, to the houses, or to the school, where we were later, that school in Prizren by the student dormitory. On those locations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Witness K41. Mr. Ryneveld, we should clarify how many bodies were buried in this grave in Zur.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us, Witness, that you collected bodies of women and children and left the men. Are you able to give the Court an estimate of how many bodies that you collected from the village of Trnje which were subsequently buried in the bush area outside of Zur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in Trnje to collect the dead, I already said that most had been collected already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K41 [Resumed]
